Dead code elimination is an optimization technique where the compiler removes code that may be executed but has no effect on the program’s behavior.

Consider a program where variable x is defined and initialized, but it is never used anywhere. It has no effect on the program’s observable behavior. Dead code elimination would remove the definition of x.
